Good Tuesday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 572 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚽ Breaking: The U.S. will host soccer's 2028 Copa América, with teams from North, Central and South America, plus the Caribbean. Host cities for the summer tournament will be announced later. Go deeper.
 
 
1 big thing: The Nvidia saga is short on answers
 
Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photo: Jose Sarmento Matos/Bloomberg via Getty Images

We still don't know why Nvidia's board ousted Jensen Huang. We also don't know why it rehired him, Axios' Dan Primack writes.

  • All of the celebration and condemnation are educated guesses at best and ignorant noise at worst.

Was he fired because... He was sleeping with an alleged spy? He was sleeping with a major customer? He was sleeping with a direct report? Other employees too? He lied to the board? He shared sensitive information with someone he shouldn't? He sidestepped U.S. export controls? He was at serious risk of prosecution? Fears of investor lawsuits?

Was he reinstated because... She definitely wasn't a spy? President Trump promised that Jensen wouldn't be prosecuted, or that he'd get a preemptive pardon? Other political pressures? The value destruction was too great? Board members were being ostracized? Employees adored him? Fears of investor lawsuits?

🤔 There have been reports and speculation about all of the above, but we don't actually know any of it.

  • The resignation and reinstatement announcements were bereft of such details, despite the trillions of dollars that moved on these choices.

Go deeper.
 
 
2. 🧑‍⚖️ Scoop: ACLU eyes court flips
 
Illustration: Allie Carl/Axios

The American Civil Liberties Union is expanding its state Supreme Court election fight into deep-red territory after the midterms left Texas just one judicial seat away from a Democratic majority, the group tells Axios' Russell Contreras exclusively.

  • The next battles over abortion, voting rights, redistricting, religion in schools and LGBTQ protections could hinge on state Supreme Court races that are often overshadowed by federal campaigns.

👀 By the numbers: The ACLU's chief political and advocacy officer Deirdre Schifeling tells Axios that it's eyeing Supreme Court races in 11 states in 2027 and 2028.

  • The group worked on court elections in five states this year.
  • It spent $30 million on its broader electoral program, with Supreme Court races claiming the biggest share.

How a small lab is giving more patients next-day answers
 
 

A kidney disease diagnosis is hard enough without a long wait for answers.

As case loads grow at Arkana Labs, they’re using Claude to help process referral paperwork with 97–98% accuracy, so patients still get results the day after a biopsy.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
President Trump pardons "Freedom" the turkey at the White House today. Photo: Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images
  1. 🦃 President Trump pardoned turkeys "Freedom" and "Feathers" today after praising his White House ballroom project and delivering a rally-style speech. Go deeper.
  2. 💥 The U.S. Army plans to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa tomorrow after getting approval from a federal appeals court — the latest in a saga that has confused and alarmed locals. Go deeper.
  3. 🆘 Microsoft declared a "Code Red" to change how it responds to major outages, Reuters reports. That's after Outlook, Teams and other popular workplace apps went down for 24 hours earlier this month. Go deeper.
  4. 🔭 Scientists have discovered the most distant quasar yet — the core of a galaxy with a black hole at its center dating back to nearly the dawn of the universe. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 📸 Pic to go: Lights-out football
 
Photo: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP

The lights at Maryland's Northwest Stadium went out during the third quarter of last night's NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders, leading to a four-minute delay.

  • The Commanders were in the red zone, trailing 10-7, when the stadium went dark.

💡 ESPN said a stadium vendor didn't disable the regular maintenance scheduled for 10 p.m. ET on weekdays.

  • After a brief timeout, the lights came back on and the game resumed. The Commanders eventually won 22-20 on a walk-off field goal.
